paper.title: A Near-Optimal Best-of-Both-Worlds Algorithm for Online Learning with Feedback Graphs

settings.name_in_paper: Online learning with a fixed directed feedback graph, adversarial regime
unmapped: Directed graph with self-loops on every vertex
Learner knows the graph and its strong independence number tilde_alpha (used in learning rate and exploration), not just the independence number
settings.definition_quote: We consider directed feedback graphs with self-loops, meaning that $(i, i) \in E$ for each vertex $i \in V$. The feedback received by the learner at the end of round $t$ is $\big\{ (i,\ell_{t,i}) \,:\, i \in \Nout(I_t) \big\}$ ... For each arm $ i \in V$, $\ell_{t, i} \in [0,1]$ for $t \ge 1$. In the adversarial regime the losses are generated arbitrarily by an oblivious adversary.

settings.name_in_paper: Online learning with a fixed directed feedback graph, stochastic regime
unmapped: Directed graph with self-loops on every vertex
Learner knows the graph and its strong independence number tilde_alpha
settings.definition_quote: In the stochastic regime they are independently drawn from a fixed but unknown distribution with expectation $\mathbb{E}[\ell_{1, i}]$.

unmapped: Graphs are directed with self-loops; graph G_t observed at the beginning of round t
settings.definition_quote: We consider a setting, where an oblivious adversary chooses a feedback graph at each round and the algorithm observes the graph at the beginning of the round.

unmapped: Graphs are directed with self-loops; graph G_t observed at the beginning of round t
settings.definition_quote: We consider a setting, where an oblivious adversary chooses a feedback graph at each round and the algorithm observes the graph at the beginning of the round. In the stochastic regime, the knowledge of the full feedback graph is required at the beginning of the round in order to construct the exploration set.

algorithms.name: EXP3.G++ (adaptive learning rate, lambda = 1, time-varying graphs)

symbols.alpha_tilde: strong independence number of G (independence number of the subgraph keeping only bidirected edges)

source.label: th:adv
source.quote: Assume that Algorithm~\ref{alg:exp3G++} is run with a directed feedback graph $G = (V,E)$, a learning rate $\eta_t = \sqrt{\frac{\ln K}{2 \tilde \alpha t}}$ and the exploration rate defined in~\eqref{eq:def_eti}--\eqref{eq:def_xiti} with $\lambda = \tilde\alpha$, $\gamma = 4$, and $\beta = 320$. Then the pseudo-regret against any oblivious loss sequence satisfies $\mathcal{R}_T \leq 4 \sqrt{\tilde \alpha T \ln K} + K$

results.notes: Regret defined as E[sum loss] - min_i E[sum loss_i], i.e. pseudo-regret. Learning rate does not depend on T, so anytime. Informal Theorem 1 restates this and Theorem 3.

symbols.Q_ind: max over strongly independent sets Ind of G of sum_{i in Ind, Delta_i>0} 1/Delta_i

source.label: th:stoc
source.quote: Let $G = (V, E)$ be a directed feedback graph with $K = |V|$ and a strong independence number $\tilde \alpha$. Under the same conditions as in Theorem~\ref{th:adv}, the pseudo-regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg:exp3G++} against any stochastic stochastic loss sequence, satisfies: \mathcal{R}_T \leq \max_{\mathrm{Ind} \in \mathcal{I}(G)} \{ \sum_{i \in \mathrm{Ind} : \Delta_i > 0} \frac{4\beta (\ln T)^2}{\Delta_{i}}\} + 2 \tilde \alpha\ln T + \frac{81 \beta K}{\Dmin^2} \ln(\frac{6\beta^2 K^2}{\Dmin^4}) + \sum_{i : \Delta_i > 0} \frac{4 \tilde \alpha}{\Delta_i}.

results.notes: beta = 320 substituted: 4*beta = 1280, 81*beta = 25920, 6*beta^2 = 614400. Same algorithm/run as Theorem 2 (best of both worlds).

symbols.sum_alpha_t: sum_{t=1}^T alpha_t, where alpha_t is the independence number of G_t

conditions: sequence of directed graphs with self-loops chosen obliviously, observed at start of each round
tuning: eta_t = sqrt(ln K / (2 sum_{s=K}^{t-1} theta_s)), theta_s = sum_i p_{s,i}/P_{s,i}

source.label: th:adv_time_var
source.quote: Assume that Algorithm~\ref{alg:exp3G++} is run on a sequence of arbitrarily generated feedback graphs $G_1, G_2, \dots$ with learning rate $\eta_t = \sqrt{\frac{\ln K}{2\sum_{s = K}^{t-1}\theta_s}} $ and exploration rates ... with $\lambda = 1$, $\gamma = 4$ and $\beta = 320$. Then the pseudo-regret against any oblivious loss sequence satisfies \mathcal{R}_T \leq 9 \sqrt{\ln K} \sqrt{\ln \lr{KT}} \sqrt{\sum_{t = 1}^T \alpha_t} + 2K

results.notes: Adaptive learning rate; algorithm does not need independence numbers.

bound.expression_latex: \inf_{0 \leq n \leq T} \lrc{ \max_{S \subset V: |S| = \tilde \alpha_n } \lrc{ \sum_{i \in S: \Delta_i > 0} \frac{4\beta \ln^2 T}{\Delta_{i}}} + n} + 2 \ln T + \sum_{i: \Delta_i > 0} \frac{16 K}{\Delta_i} + \frac{181 \beta K^{3/2}}{\Dmin^2} \lr{\ln\lr{\frac{20\beta^2 K^{5/2}}{\Dmin^4}}}^2

symbols.B_inf: inf_{0<=n<=T} { max_{S subset V, |S| = tilde_alpha_n} sum_{i in S, Delta_i>0} 1280 ln^2 T / Delta_i + n }
symbols.tilde_alpha_n: n-th largest strong independence number among G_1..G_T

conditions: sequence of directed graphs with self-loops chosen obliviously, observed at start of each round

source.label: th:adv_time_var
source.quote: Simultaneously, the pseudo-regret against stochastic losses satisfies: R_T \leq \inf_{0 \leq n \leq T} \{ \max_{S \subset V: |S| = \tilde \alpha_n } \{ \sum_{i \in S: \Delta_i > 0} \frac{4\beta \ln^2 T}{\Delta_{i}}\} + n\} + 2 \ln T + \sum_{i: \Delta_i > 0} \frac{16 K}{\Delta_i} + \frac{181 \beta K^{3/2}}{\Dmin^2} (\ln(\frac{20\beta^2 K^{5/2}}{\Dmin^4}))^2
